claims.text: The proposed alloy system is AlxCrCoFeNi with target compositions near x = 0.1 and x = 0.5.
Melt-processed AlxCrCoFeNi initially forms a largely chemically disordered solid solution.
High-strain compression can induce increased chemical ordering in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
High-pressure torsion induces enhanced SRO or clustering in AlxCrCoFeNi.
Rapid quenching produces an AlxCrCoFeNi baseline with high chemical disorder and no significant SRO or clustering.
The extent and character of local SRO and clustering can be quantified using atom probe tomography, TEM, and neutron diffraction.
Enhanced SRO creates local regions of chemical clustering.
Chemical clustering in AlxCrCoFeNi generates internal stress fields.
Clustering-generated stress fields impede both edge and screw dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases hardness and yield strength.
High-pressure torsion substantially increases the hardness and strength of Al0.5CoCrFeNi.
SRO-inducing processing will increase hardness and yield strength relative to a rapidly quenched baseline.
The expected increase in hardness and yield strength is approximately 20–30%.
Mechanical enhancement will correlate quantitatively with the measured extent of SRO after grain refinement and phase changes are controlled.
AlxCrCoFeNi exhibits substantial chemical clustering for Al contents below x = 0.5 over a wide temperature range.
The proposed SRO-strengthening mechanism is most effective for x below approximately 0.5 because lattice distortion remains moderate.
The hypothesis should hold from room temperature to approximately 300 °C for x approximately 0.1–0.5.
At higher temperatures or more extreme compositions, phase transformations or grain refinement may supersede SRO as the dominant source of strength.
Refinement of a second phase during HPT is a plausible competing explanation for strengthening in Al0.5CoCrFeNi.
Failure to observe a statistically significant strength and hardness increase that tracks SRO, or stronger tracking with grain refinement or phase changes, would falsify SRO as the primary mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes high-strain processing as producing both enhanced ordering and clustering, while the proposed mechanism treats ordering as creating clustering. These are not clearly distinguished even though the cited Al0.1CrCoFeNi evidence describes compression as causing a clustering-to-ordering transition.
